claims.text: Refractory tungsten-based composites and high-entropy alloys are candidate structural materials for fusion plasma-facing components.
A typical unoptimized plasma-facing alloy has a conventional grain-boundary network.
High-temperature plastic strain and toughness in refractory plasma-facing alloys are primarily governed by engineered grain-boundary character.
Increasing grain-boundary coherence or semi-coherence makes boundaries effective dislocation sources and sinks.
Effective dislocation emission and absorption at engineered boundaries distributes plastic strain more evenly.
More evenly distributed plastic strain reduces local interfacial stress concentrations.
Reducing local interfacial stress concentrations blunts crack initiation and delays crack propagation.
Heat treatment and minor alloying can tailor grain-boundary chemistry and structure toward greater coherence and favorable interface character.
Grain and phase interfaces influence local plastic-strain distribution and dislocation interactions.
In FeCoCrNiAl0.5, heterogeneous plastic-strain accumulation occurs near fcc–bcc/B2 phase boundaries, which act as dislocation obstacles.
Uniformly distributed TiC within tungsten grains and along grain boundaries improves high-heat-flux tolerance relative to pure tungsten.
TiC at tungsten grain boundaries strengthens the boundaries and resists grain-boundary migration at elevated temperature.
Operating above 1000 °C under high heat flux and stress is representative of fusion-reactor plasma-facing service.
The hypothesized behavior applies where grain-boundary-mediated deformation dominates over irradiation damage and bulk phase transformations.
Engineered-boundary samples should have more homogeneous strain distributions than conventionally processed samples under matched high-temperature loading.
Engineered-boundary samples should sustain greater plastic strain before failure than the baseline.
Engineered-boundary samples should exhibit greater crack blunting and fracture toughness than the baseline.
The grain-boundary hypothesis can be isolated by comparing otherwise identical samples with conventional and optimized grain-boundary structures under the same cyclic thermal and mechanical loading.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant improvement exceeding 10% in distributed plastic deformation and fracture toughness would falsify the hypothesis.
A finding that engineered boundaries do not markedly affect dislocation arrangements or dynamics would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The experiment says the two sample sets differ only in grain-boundary structure, but the intervention includes alloying adjustments. Changing alloy content also changes composition and may alter phases, precipitates, and bulk properties, so the proposed comparison would not necessarily isolate grain-boundary structure.
